    40	
    41	## Funder observations
    42	
    43	`funders.parquet` represents source-role observations, not resolved people or
    44	companies. Each row includes member, declaration, and register IDs, a role, a
    45	scope, and a JSON pointer into the declaration's retained raw source.
    46	
    47	| Scope | Identity | Funding reference |
    48	| --- | --- | --- |
    49	| `funding_entry` | `<funding_entry_id>/<role>` | Non-null funding ID and ordinal. |
    50	| `declaration` | `<member UUID>/<declaration ID>/<register ID>/declaration/<role>` | Null funding ID and ordinal. |
    51	
    52	Declaration observations retain latest top-level names and donor metadata when
    53	those fields have no `Value` or `PaymentType` funding anchor. They can coexist
    54	with nested funding entries. A top-level funding occurrence supplies its own
    55	observations without an additional declaration observation.
    56	
    57	Roles are `donor`, `payer`, and `ultimate_payer`. Only donor observations receive
    58	`donor_kind` and `donor_company_number`. The cleaner does not select a preferred
    59	role, propagate parent names to child declarations, or reconcile company-number
    60	conflicts. Two matching names still have distinct observation IDs, including
    61	confidential names.
    62	
    63	## Name features
    64	
    65	All features are independent candidates for future resolution. No feature is an
    66	entity ID or a reason to merge rows.
    67	
    68	| Column | Rule |
    69	| --- | --- |
    70	| `name_raw` | Original string, including punctuation, whitespace, and placeholders. |
    71	| `name_status` | `missing` for absent or whitespace-only names; `withheld` for the exact normalized placeholders listed below; otherwise `present`. |
    72	| `name_normalized` | Unicode NFKC, Unicode lowercase, and trimmed, collapsed whitespace. Includes parenthetical and geographic text. |
    73	| `name_accent_folded` | NFD decomposition of the normalized name with combining marks removed. No transliteration. |
    74	| `name_tokens` | Normalized full name with ampersands converted to `and`, apostrophes joined, single-letter dotted acronyms joined, and other punctuation converted to token boundaries. |
    75	| `name_token_key` | Lexically sorted tokens, including repeated tokens. |
    76	| `primary_name_normalized` | Normalized name excluding explicit trading-as text and parenthetical trading-as annotations. Other parentheses remain. |
    77	| `organisation_core` | Primary-name tokens with one complete trailing UK legal suffix removed. |
    78	| `person_core` | Full-name tokens with listed leading honorifics removed. |
    79	| `person_initials` | First character of each person-core token. |
    80	| `organisation_initials` | First character of each organisation-core token, excluding listed connective words. |
    81	| `parenthetical_text` | Original contents of outer parentheses, in source order. An unmatched opening retains the remaining text. |
    82	| `explicit_aliases` | Original names following a literal `trading as` or `t/a` marker. Parenthetical markers do not also create whole-string aliases. |
    83	| `alias_normalized` | NFKC, lowercase, and whitespace-normalized forms of the explicit aliases. |
    84	| `explicit_acronym` | An uppercase source acronym of 2 to 10 letters, allowing dots and whitespace, whose lowercase letters match the connective-free initials of its parenthetical expansion. Expansion before the acronym is also supported. |
    85	| `acronym_expansion_normalized` | Normalized full expansion of a validated explicit acronym. |
    86	| `has_conjunction` | A literal `and` token or ampersand. Does not assert multiple entities. |
    87	| `has_unbalanced_parentheses` | An unmatched opening or closing parenthesis. |
    88	
    89	Exact withheld placeholders are `confidential`, `withheld`, `name withheld`,
    90	`anonymous`, and `not disclosed`. Missing and withheld names retain `name_raw` and
    91	their status but have no primary matching features.
    92	
    93	Legal suffixes are `limited`, `ltd`, `plc`, `llp`, `lp`, `cic`, `public limited
    94	company`, `community interest company`, `limited liability partnership`, and
    95	`limited partnership`. Removal requires a whole trailing token sequence. Leading
    96	honorifics are `mr`, `mrs`, `ms`, `miss`, `mx`, `dr`, `prof`, `professor`, `sir`,
    97	`dame`, `lord`, `lady`, `rev`, `reverend`, `rt`, and `hon`. Connective words for
    98	organisation initials and acronym checks are `a`, `an`, `and`, `for`, `in`, `of`,
    99	`on`, `the`, and `to`.
   100	
   101	| Original name | Selected features |
   102	| --- | --- |
   103	| `Labour Together Limited` and `LABOUR TOGETHER LTD.` | Both organisation cores are `labour together`. Observation IDs remain distinct. |
   104	| `National  Liberal Club` | Normalized name is `national liberal club`. |
   105	| `James O’Brien` | Tokens are `james obrien`. Raw and normalized names retain the apostrophe. |
   106	| `Friends of Sinn Féin Canada` | Accent-folded name is `friends of sinn fein canada`. Full-name features retain `canada`. |
   107	| `CSC Computer Sciences Limited (Trading as DXC Technology Ltd)` | Primary organisation core is `csc computer sciences`; explicit alias is `DXC Technology Ltd`. Full-name tokens keep the annotation. |
   108	| `ASLEF (Associated Society of Locomotive Engineers and Firemen)` | Explicit acronym is `aslef` with the full normalized expansion. |
   109	| `BJD (GB) Limited` | Organisation core is `bjd gb`. The cleaner does not drop `GB` or infer it as an acronym. |
   110	| `Alan Milburn & Ruth Briel` | Conjunction indicator is true. The cleaner does not split people. |
   111	| `MPM Connect Ltd (a company controlled by Peter Hearn)` | Parenthetical evidence remains. There is no inferred alias for Peter Hearn. |
   112	
   113	There is no fuzzy matching, phonetic encoding, external enrichment, or inferred
   114	entity-type selection. The original donor kind remains available beside the
   115	parallel person and organisation features.
import pytest

from exposed.adapters.declaration_models import SourceDeclaration
from exposed.core.errors import DeclarationParseError
from tests.declaration_fakes import declaration, field, money


def parse(fields):
    return SourceDeclaration.model_validate(declaration(fields=fields)).to_draft().accept()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "name,expected",
    [
        ("UNITE The Union", "unite the union"),
        ("ÉXAMPLE", "éxample"),
        ("Example Limited", "example ltd"),
        ("Example LTD", "example ltd"),
        ("Example Ltd.", "example ltd"),
        (" \tExample LiMiTeD\n ", "example ltd"),
        ("\tExample LTD.\u00a0", "example ltd"),
        ("  Example  Donor  ", "example  donor"),
        ("Example  Limited", "example  ltd"),
        ("Example\tLimited", "example\tltd"),
        ("Limited", "ltd"),
        ("Limited Edition", "limited edition"),
        ("Example Ltd. Holdings", "example ltd. holdings"),
        ("Example Unlimited", "example unlimited"),
        ("ExampleLimited", "examplelimited"),
        ("Example Limited.", "example limited."),
        (" \t\n", None),
        (None, None),
    ],
)
def test_funder_names_are_standardized(name, expected):
    result = parse([field("DonorName", name), money()])
    assert result.funding[0].funder_name == expected
    assert result.payer == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["UltimatePayerName", "DonorName", "PayerName", "Name"])
def test_all_funder_name_fields_are_standardized(name):
    fields = [field(name, "  Example LIMITED  "), money()]
    if name == "Name":
        fields = [field("Donors", None, "Donor[]", values=[fields])]
    assert parse(fields).funding[0].funder_name == "example ltd"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "status,number,expected",
    [
        ("Company", "00123456", "00123456"),
        ("Company", "OC012345", "OC012345"),
        ("Company", None, None),
        ("Company", "  ", None),
        ("Individual", "00123456", None),
        ("Trade Union", "00123456", None),
        ("Future status", None, None),
        (None, "00123456", None),
        ("", None, None),
    ],
)
def test_explicit_donor_fields_preserve_source_status_and_company_identifiers(
    status, number, expected
):
    result = parse(
        [
            field("DonorName", "Donor"),
            money(),
            field("DonorStatus", status),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", number),
        ]
    ).funding[0]
    assert result.funder_kind == (status or None)
    assert result.company_number == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["DonorStatus", "DonorCompanyIdentifier"])
def test_invalid_metadata_rejects_declaration_instead_of_coercing_numbers(name):
    fields = [field("DonorName", "Donor"), money(), field("DonorStatus", "Company")]
    if name == "DonorStatus":
        fields[-1]["value"] = 123
    else:
        fields.append(field(name, 123))
    with pytest.raises(DeclarationParseError, match="expected a string"):
        parse(fields)


def test_donor_groups_keep_metadata_paired_without_inheriting_outer_fields():
    result = parse(
        [
            field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "99999999"),
            field(
                "Donors",
                None,
                "Donor[]",
                values=[
                    [field("Name", "Person"), field("DonorStatus", "Individual"), money()],
                    [
                        field("Name", "Company"),
                        field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
                        field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "00123456"),
                        money(),
                    ],
                    [
                        field("Name", "Unknown"),
                        field("IsPrivateIndividual", False, "Boolean"),
                        money(),
                    ],
                ],
            ),
        ]
    )
    assert [(e.funder_name, e.funder_kind, e.company_number) for e in result.funding] == [
        ("person", "Individual", None),
        ("company", "Company", "00123456"),
        ("unknown", None, None),
    ]


def test_donor_metadata_is_not_attached_to_a_different_ultimate_payer():
    result = parse(
        [
            field("UltimatePayerName", "Another funder"),
            field("DonorName", "Intermediary"),
            field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "00123456"),
            money(),
        ]
    ).funding[0]
    assert result.funder_name == "another funder"
    assert result.funder_kind is result.company_number is None


def test_donor_metadata_applies_to_the_same_standardized_ultimate_payer():
    result = parse(
        [
            field("UltimatePayerName", " EXAMPLE LTD. "),
            field("DonorName", "Example Limited"),
            field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "SC001234"),
            money(),
        ]
    ).funding[0]
    assert result.funder_name == "example ltd"
    assert result.funder_kind == "Company"
    assert result.company_number == "SC001234"


def test_latest_publication_supplies_metadata():
    from copy import deepcopy

    source = declaration(
        fields=[field("DonorName", "Donor"), money(), field("DonorStatus", "Company")]
    )
    older = deepcopy(source["versions"][0])
    older["register"]["publishedDate"] = "2023-01-01"
    older["fields"][-1]["value"] = "Individual"
    source["versions"].insert(0, older)
    assert SourceDeclaration.model_validate(source).to_draft().funding[0].funder_kind == "Company"

def test_invalid_metadata_rejects_declaration_instead_of_coercing_numbers(name):
    fields = [field("DonorName", "Donor"), money(), field("DonorStatus", "Company")]
    if name == "DonorStatus":
        fields[-1]["value"] = 123
    else:
        fields.append(field(name, 123))
    with pytest.raises(DeclarationParseError, match="expected a string"):
        parse(fields)


def test_donor_groups_keep_metadata_paired_without_inheriting_outer_fields():
    result = parse(
        [
            field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "99999999"),
            field(
                "Donors",
                None,
                "Donor[]",
                values=[
                    [field("Name", "Person"), field("DonorStatus", "Individual"), money()],
                    [
                        field("Name", "Company"),
                        field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
                        field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "00123456"),
                        money(),
                    ],
                    [
                        field("Name", "Unknown"),
                        field("IsPrivateIndividual", False, "Boolean"),
                        money(),
                    ],
                ],
            ),
        ]
    )
    assert [(e.funder_name, e.funder_kind, e.company_number) for e in result.funding] == [

        ("company", "Company", "00123456"),
        ("unknown", None, None),

    result = parse(
        [
            field("UltimatePayerName", "Another funder"),
            field("DonorName", "Intermediary"),
            field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "00123456"),
            money(),
        ]
    ).funding[0]
    assert result.funder_name == "another funder"
    assert result.funder_kind is result.company_number is None


def test_donor_metadata_applies_to_the_same_standardized_ultimate_payer():
    result = parse(
        [
            field("UltimatePayerName", " EXAMPLE LTD. "),
            field("DonorName", "Example Limited"),
            field("DonorStatus", "Company"),
            field("DonorCompanyIdentifier", "SC001234"),
            money(),
        ]
    ).funding[0]
    assert result.funder_name == "example ltd"
    assert result.funder_kind == "Company"
    assert result.company_number == "SC001234"

    from copy import deepcopy

    source = declaration(
        fields=[field("DonorName", "Donor"), money(), field("DonorStatus", "Company")]

1-# Declaration ingestion
2-
3:Updated on 24 September 2026: funders are now stored in `funders`, shared by exact
4:source name, with `funder_kind` and `company_number` on that record. Funding entries
5:reference its UUID through nullable `funder_id`; unnamed payments keep a null
6:reference. This supersedes the original per-entry funder storage and no-sharing
7:policy below. Explicit incoming metadata updates the shared funder, missing fields
8-preserve known details, and a non-company kind clears a previous company number.
9:Metadata-only funder changes preserve payment UUIDs. Payment or attribution changes
10-still replace the entire funding group. All changes remain atomic per MP. See
11:[the current ingestion rules](../../ingest/README.md#funder-identification).
12-
13-Updated on 17 September 2026: declaration writes commit after each MP, and the selected
14-version's nullable `registrationDate` is stored as `registration_date`. The single development
--
16-
17-## Problem Statement
18-
19:Exposed currently imports members and their Commons service into PostgreSQL, but it cannot yet import the financial declarations needed for later display. The original donation sketch assumes a donor and an amount per record. Parliament's declarations are broader: they include nonfinancial disclosures, declarations with several funders, in-kind benefits, and payments whose payer information belongs to a related declaration.
20-
21-The project needs a simple model that links declarations to their source IDs, exposes useful funding fields, and extends the current Pydantic-based importer without taking ownership of member updates. Repeated imports must update existing declarations consistently. A malformed amount must be diagnosable through logs and must not leave a declaration with only some of its funding imported.
22-
--
26-
27-Store one declaration record per source declaration ID, linked directly to the existing member, with its readable category, source registration date and retrieval time. Persist only parsed fields; do not store raw source JSON. Store zero or more funding entries separately, each with its own UUID and the source declaration ID that groups it with its declaration.
28-
29:Funding entries expose the source funder, exact decimal amount, currency, and payment type. Prefer an explicitly supplied ultimate payer; otherwise use the source donor or payer, resolving the parent declaration when required. Store the selected name without retaining alternative payer identities or attempting to identify shared donors across declarations.
30-

*** Add File: /Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/.design/funder-resolution/why-investigation.md
+# Funder resolution: historical constraints
+
+## Question and anchor
+
+Why does the current cleaner preserve separate observations and emit matching features without resolving identities, and what can the older importer teach the proposed resolution CLI?
+
+Baseline: `main` at `9e4de95`. Anchors: `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:41`, `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_cleaning.rs:90`, `funder_name.rs:1`, and `exposed/src/lib/inbound/cli.rs:92`. The Python `ingest/src/exposed/declaration_importer.py` is now a compatibility entry point; its attribution policy lives in `core/declarations.py` and persistence in `adapters/declaration_postgres.py`.
+
+## What we found
+
+- **Direct rationale:** PR #22 states that raw capture combines declaration, funding and funder evidence, and introduces an offline cleaning step for separate funding entries and observations “with feature columns for later entity resolution.” Its tradeoff says: “Equal name features can support later matching without prematurely merging people or organisations.” This explicitly answers why equality does not merge observations. Author: `johnnylarner`, 7 October 2026. [PR #22](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/22).
+- **Direct scope:** The same PR says: “Entity resolution, parent attribution and database loading remain separate stages.” This is a boundary of that cleaning change, not a permanent prohibition on adding resolution. [PR #22](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/22).
+- **Direct documented policy:** The cleaner's reference defines roles and scopes, retains source pointers, assigns donor metadata only to donor observations, and says matching names remain distinct. Features are candidates, never entity IDs. Missing and withheld names carry no primary matching features. `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:43–66,89–91`.
+- **Direct documented legacy limitation:** The Python importer's shared normalized name is “a storage key, not verified identity matching.” Its database model reuses a UUID for repeated standardized names, updates explicit metadata with the last imported value, and retains omitted metadata. `ingest/README.md:74–78,120–137`; `adapters/declaration_postgres.py:86–108`. These document behavior, not a reason that exact-name identity is safe.
+- **Direct historical design context:** The old specification says financial declarations include several funders, in-kind benefits and parent-held payer information. It chose a simple model for useful financial fields, selecting the ultimate payer rather than retaining alternative payer identities. Source examples informed that model; an ultimate-payer payment and a parent-payer payment are explicitly cited as evidence for preserving parent relationships. Historical `docs/specs/declaration-ingestion.md` at `4d71106:17–29,239–244` (the file is absent on current main).
+- **Supported policy continuity, not proof of identity:** Tests cover ultimate-payer preference, preserving donor-group metadata, refusing donor metadata for a different ultimate payer, and sharing names without collapsing payments. This converges with the documentation on a single attributed payer plus exact-name storage design. `ingest/tests/test_funder_identification.py:95–148`, `test_funder_storage.py:19–40`, `core/declarations.py:47–64`.
+- **Direct history:** #9 restored name normalization from `95ab25b`; its body gives no explanation beyond recovery. #8 adds shared funder identities but has an empty PR body. #17 has no descriptive body and its only inline review says “We don't need this” on README.md; this is about that documentation, not an entity-resolution policy. [PR #9](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/9), [PR #8](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/8), [PR #17 review](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/17#discussion_r4173930815).
+
+## Reasonable inference
+
+- **Inferred:** Separate observations appear to make later decisions auditable and revisable: source IDs and pointers survive, while multiple interpretations of names are available in parallel. #22 explicitly postpones merges; the cleaner reference supplies the traceability machinery. Reversibility as an author motivation is not separately stated.
+- **Inferred:** Legacy ultimate-payer preference appears aimed at reporting who ultimately funded a payment in a compact display model. The historical problem statement, selected-name design and source examples support that reading. It does not justify discarding donor or intermediary evidence in a new resolution stage.
+- **Inferred:** Exact-name sharing was likely a pragmatic storage simplification. The docs explicitly disclaim verified matching and tests exercise UUID reuse. No source inspected explains why exact standardized name was preferred over company numbers or probabilistic resolution.
+
+## Unknowns and competing explanations
+
+We found no documented accuracy target, fuzzy threshold, approved clustering rule, adjudication workflow, external registry policy or collision-handling rationale. Neither #8 nor #9 records why its precise normalization rules were chosen. Simplicity and historical implementation convenience both fit exact-name sharing; the record does not distinguish them. #22 records reported verification counts but supplies no measured entity-resolution precision or recall.
+
+The legacy name-sharing contract differs from the current observation contract. This is a change of stage and output meaning, not evidence that current observations should inherit legacy UUID equality or last-write-wins metadata.
+
+## Sources consulted and coverage
+
+- **Source control:** Path histories for cleaner models/docs and legacy importer; commit messages/details for `9e4de95`, `6d41414`, `46b792a`, `5f4c05a`, `34a4de8`, `4d71106`, `eef6697`; historical spec at `4d71106`; current docs, domain comments, CLI and named tests. Queries: `git log --oneline -- <paths>`, `git show -s --format=fuller <commits>`, `git show <commit>:<path>`, `rg 'funder|identify|match|ultimate|preferred|exact'`. Read PR bodies/reviews #22/#17 and inline comments through `gh`; followed legacy history to #8/#9. No implementation executed.
+- **Issue tracker:** Skipped under the explicit teach investigation scope (git, repository docs/tests and relevant PRs). #16 appears in #17's commit message but was not opened.
+- **Long-form documents:** Repository documentation above searched. External document connectors skipped under the explicit narrowed scope; no unrelated personal documents queried.
+- **Real-time team chat:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope.
+- **Infrastructure observability:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope.
+- **Error/exception tracking:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope.
+- **Product analytics warehouse:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope; no database access or queries.
+
+## Planning constraints
+
+- **Preserve:** Raw evidence, observation identities, role/scope/source pointers, repeated funding occurrences and absent/withheld status. Keep donor metadata attached to its source role. These are documented cleaner contracts, not future entity decisions.
+- **Change:** Add an explicit resolution stage whose results link observations to proposed or accepted entities. Treat cleaner features as evidence inputs. The separate-stage boundary in #22 permits this extension without changing what cleaner IDs mean.
+- **Avoid:** Reusing legacy normalized-name uniqueness as proof of real identity; erasing source observations when names match; attributing donor company numbers to other roles; treating all confidential placeholders as one person; interpreting controller text or conjunctions as automatic aliases/splits. `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:57–66,89–111` and legacy metadata tests provide the evidence for these constraints.
+- **Risk:** False merges can spread transitively through weaker aliases, initials or common names; exact company-number conflicts and conflicting donor kinds need an explicit policy; resolution must distinguish identifying an entity from selecting which role funded a payment. These are design risks inferred from the available features and role distinctions, not recorded production incidents.
+
+## Confidence summary
+
+The cleaner's separation and deferred identity decisions have direct PR evidence. Legacy behavior and display-oriented constraints are documented, but its exact matching policy's motivation and any safe automatic-resolution rules remain uncertain. Teaching should state those gaps before implementation.
*** End Patch"));

- **Change:** Add an explicit resolution stage whose results link observations to proposed or accepted entities. Treat cleaner features as evidence inputs. The separate-stage boundary in #22 permits this extension without changing what cleaner IDs mean.
- **Avoid:** Reusing legacy normalized-name uniqueness as proof of real identity; erasing source observations when names match; attributing donor company numbers to other roles; treating all confidential placeholders as one person; interpreting controller text or conjunctions as automatic aliases/splits. `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:57–66,89–111` and legacy metadata tests provide the evidence for these constraints.
- **Risk:** False merges can spread transitively through weaker aliases, initials or common names; exact company-number conflicts and conflicting donor kinds need an explicit policy; resolution must distinguish identifying an entity from selecting which role funded a payment. These are design risks inferred from the available features and role distinctions, not recorded production incidents.

## Confidence summary

The cleaner's separation and deferred identity decisions have direct PR evidence. Legacy behavior and display-oriented constraints are documented, but its exact matching policy's motivation and any safe automatic-resolution rules remain uncertain. Teaching should state those gaps before implementation.
